history.period: Dedicated 19 April 1923 (Akshaya Tritiya); marble statue installed 8 April 1954
history.summary: The Sri Sri Matri Mandir was built exactly on the spot where Sarada Devi (22 December 1853 – 20 July 1920), the wife and spiritual consort of Sri Ramakrishna and the Holy Mother of the Ramakrishna movement, was born. It was dedicated by Swami Saradananda on Thursday, 19 April 1923 (Akshaya Tritiya); the white marble statue of the Holy Mother was installed on 8 April 1954 along with a spacious prayer hall. The complex also preserves her old house (used c.1863–1915, where many received initiation) and the Amodar ghat; it is run by Sri Sri Matrimandir & Ramakrishna Mission Sarada Sevashrama. FLAGS: (1) CSV 'state' column wrongly holds 'Bankura' — actual state is West Bengal; (2) CSV town 'Bankura' corrected to actual town Joyrambati village (spelt Jayrambati/Jairambati); (3) a small Shiva lingam found during excavation is also worshipped in the sanctum.

name: Joyrambati Matri Mandir
town_description: Joyrambati (also spelt Jayrambati/Jairambati) is a small village in the Kotulpur block of Bankura district, West Bengal, famous as the birthplace of Holy Mother Sri Sarada Devi and as a pilgrimage centre of the Ramakrishna tradition, a few kilometres from Kamarpukur, the birthplace of Sri Ramakrishna.
